g.text: Segments, a sparse index, and the page cache - why retention deletes files, not records
rolls at log.segment.bytes = 1 GB, or log.roll.ms = 7 days
sparse index entries - one per ~4 KB (index.interval.bytes), not one per record
lookup: binary-search the index, jump to the nearest earlier byte position,
then scan forward a few KB. A dense index would not fit in memory.
Retention deletes WHOLE segments. A 1 GB segment that takes 10 days to fill
keeps data well past a 7-day retention, because it cannot be deleted until it rolls.
Why it is fast: the page cache IS the cache
sendfile(): kernel straight to socket, never through user space
JVM heap stays small - a few GB even on a 128 GB box; the rest of RAM is page cache.
A consumer far enough behind reads cold data from disk, so lag is self-reinforcing.
